page: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-2g is a specialized accelerator-optimized virtual machine tailored for deep learning, scientific simulation, and large-scale parallel processing. The server is powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, delivering 52 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 26 physical execution cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU subsystem is equipped with 105 MB of shared L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions along with AVX-512 vector instructions. System memory totals 468 GB, yielding an allocation of 9.0 GB per physical core. Accelerator hardware consists of two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing a combined 160 GB of high-bandwidth video memory. In addition to core compute and graphics resources, the instance incorporates 1608 GB of local NVMe SSD storage to accommodate rapid input and output operations for working datasets.

Empirical benchmarks demonstrate top-tier execution speed across artificial intelligence workloads. In large language model inference tests, the dual H100 setup achieves top-decile performance, processing over 10254 prompt tokens per second and generating 350 tokens per second on 135M models, while sustaining 5644 prompt tokens per second and 194 text generation tokens per second on 7B models. System memory throughput is equally resilient, logging read bandwidth exceeding 214 GB per second and write bandwidth above 92 GB per second on uncached blocks. Standard CPU benchmarks align with high-end enterprise hardware, scoring 54314.03 in PassMark CPU tests and 17415.0 in Geekbench multi-core evaluations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 302.55 GB per second, reflecting solid data ingest and transformation capability.

From a resource and efficiency standpoint, the a3-highgpu-2g configuration balances high capital hardware accessibility against full eight-way GPU clusters. By provisioning two H100 accelerators instead of an entire host chassis, it offers an entry point for teams requiring Hopper tensor architecture without paying for unneeded accelerator overhead. Tradeoffs include the absence of bundled public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated network infrastructure setup, and storage fixed to local scratch space that requires replication for persistence. The instance is optimally configured for fine-tuning medium-sized language models, real-time transformer inference, complex video processing, distributed deep learning worker nodes, and compute-heavy scientific research pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-2g is an accelerator-optimized instance engineered for computationally intensive artificial intelligence and high-performance computing tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the machine features 52 dedicated vCPUs across 26 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors running at 2.7 GHz, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AMX and AVX-512. Memory capacity stands at 468 GB, providing 9 GB per core with high uncached bandwidth. Hardware acceleration is delivered by 2 NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs offering 160 GB of combined VRAM, supplemented by 1608 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results place this configuration in the top tier for large language model inference across 135M and 7B parameter models, while maintaining strong multi-core processing and compression scores. The instance provides substantial resource density for organizations running machine learning training, real-time model inference, molecular modeling, and data-intensive simulations without requiring full multi-node cluster footprints.
